title: Defensive hire risk mitigation and staggered onboarding protocol
body:
Purpose:
This doc describes a defensive hiring pattern for mid-to-senior platform and infra hires where small mistakes or mismatches can have high operational or security blast-radius. It pairs an interview rubric that emphasizes risk signals with a staggered onboarding pathway that minimizes early duty exposure and accelerates safe ownership.

Scope and when to use this protocol:
- Roles: infra-engineer, model-serving-sre, private-deployments-eng, platform-security.
- Use when hire will have: elevated access (KMS/HSM, network config), ownership of customer-facing inference runtime, or responsibility for private/on-prem stacks.
- Not intended for purely product-facing or frontend hires (use standard onboarding).

Hiring plan (high level):
1) Intake (HR + Hiring manager): 3 business days. Clarify minimal capabilities, expected first-90d deliverables, access gating needs, and target start-of-duty date.
2) Lightweight take-home (optional for senior candidates): 48–72 hours, focused on incident reasoning and small infra code review (not full system design). Purpose: reveal risk-aware thinking.
3) Interview loop (2–4 days): blended behavioral, incident-response, architecture, and security probes.
4) Offer & staged access plan included in offer: the offer package must include a clear description of staged privileges and first-30d duty expectations.

Interview rubric (scoring guidance):
- Format: each interviewer scores 1–5 per competency, with comments. Final decision requires average >= 3.6 and no single competency <= 2.
- Competency areas (weights in parentheses):
  * Risk awareness & incident judgement (25%) — examples: tradeoff analysis under pressure, prioritization during incidents, when to roll back vs patch.
  * Systems & ops fundamentals (20%) — low-level debugging, resource limits, capacity reasoning.
  * Security and access model thinking (20%) — principle of least privilege, KMS/HSM workflows, secrets lifecycle.
  * Collaboration & communication (15%) — cross-team escalation, runbook clarity, async updates.
  * Cost-consciousness & performance tradeoffs (10%) — batching/caching decisions, cost-SLO tradeoffs.
  * Ownership maturity (10%) — history of safe rollouts, postmortem quality.

Scoring rubric (quick cheat-sheet):
- 5 = exceptional: cites concrete examples, quantifies impact, shows pattern-based solutions and mitigations.
- 4 = strong: clear reasoning, minor gaps in depth.
- 3 = acceptable: solid fundamentals, needs mentoring on emergent risks.
- 2 = concerning: misses obvious safety tradeoffs or lacks incident examples.
- 1 = fail: would create high-probability high-impact risk without heavy oversight.

Red flags (immediate blocker unless clearly mitigated):
- No concrete incident ownership history for operations roles.
- Dismissive attitude toward least-privilege or auditability.
- Vague answers on handling live customer data exposure.

Staggered onboarding checklist (staged privileges and milestones) — first 90 days broken into safe phases:
Phase 0 — Pre-start (offer signed):
- HR sends staged-access agreement explaining progressive privileges and expected readiness checkpoints.
- Manager files pod-level access plan and emergency-elevations protocol with SRE lead.
- IT schedules laptop with encryption + approved baseline images; KMS onboarding scheduled but not provisioned.

Phase 1 — Days 0–14 (shadow & orient, minimal access):
- No prod write access to inference runtimes. Read-only dashboards + aggregated logs only.
- Complete orientation: security training, privacy rules, codebase map, developer sandbox.
- Buddy assignment: 1:1 with a senior engineer for daily check-ins (first week).
- Deliverable: safe checklist walkthrough and a short runbook summary for a non-production service.

Phase 2 — Days 15–45 (incremental responsibilities):
- Limited, scoped deploy rights to staging environments.
- Introduce to incident playbooks; run a simulated postmortem exercise with team.
- Empowered to make non-production configuration changes after peer review.
- Deliverable: lead a staging incident drill and submit a mini postmortem.

Phase 3 — Days 46–90 (conditional production exposure):
- Controlled, time-bound production change window with two approvers; elevated access via short-lived tokens.
- Candidate must complete security checklist and have two positive technical endorsements.
- Deliverable: safely deploy a minor improvement with documented rollback plan and performance validation.

Post-90d (regular cadence): full access reviews at 3- and 6-month marks; automatic audit triggers for privilege expansion.

Acceptance thresholds and contingencies:
- Hire passes probation if milestones at Phase 1–3 completed and engineering + security endorsements recorded.
- If any major safety concern arises during Phase 1–3, manager escalates to People Ops + Security; options: extended shadow period, targeted remediation plan (30 days), or termination.

Offer language suggestions (short blurb to include):
"To protect customer data and operational reliability, your onboarding will follow a staged-access pathway: read-only orientation, supervised staging responsibilities, then conditional production privileges after documented readiness checks. This is a standard practice for roles with elevated access."

Onboarding checklists and templates (copyable items):
- First-24hrs checklist: account creation, laptop image, team intro, buddy calendar invites, security training link.
- First-week tasks: read runbooks, access dashboards (RO), attend incident simulation, complete compliance form.
- First-30d: staging deploy walk-through, submit mini-postmortem, peer-reviewed PR.
- 60–90d: production deploy with two approvers, cost-impact signoff, performance validation.

Runbook & simulation exercises (examples to use in interviews/onboarding):
- Exercise 1: "KV cache regression" — candidate receives a timeline of degraded tail latency after a model rollout; asked to triage, propose mitigation steps, and outline postmortem.
- Exercise 2: "Secrets drift" — an internal process rotated a secret; one service failed silently. Candidate outlines detection, remediation, and controls to prevent recurrence.

Manager responsibilities checklist (to reduce risk):
- Prepares access gating and documents emergency escalation.
- Assigns a senior buddy and sets daily catchups for 2 weeks.
- Prepares at least two staged tasks with rollback paths for Phase 2 and Phase 3.

People Ops responsibilities checklist:
- Attach staged-access agreement to offer and ensure candidate signs it.
- Coordinate background checks where required.
- Record privileged access timeline and store in audit log.

Security & compliance tie-ins:
- All elevated access expansions must be reviewed by Security and logged in the central access control system.
- Automated alerts should be configured to tag any first-time production deploys by the new hire for 72 hours.

Contingency flows (quick notes):
- Candidate declines offer before start: HR runs a 1:1 to capture reasons, logs signals for future sourcing.
- Early exit in Phase 1–2: preserve ramp notes, immediately revoke any temporary credentials, and run a handoff with buddy.
- Post-hire incident with contributor involvement: require expedited postmortem and remedial training before privilege restoration.

Open questions & next steps (work-in-progress):
- Devise a short, standardized security quiz for Phase 1 graduation.
- Automate the staged access timeline in onboarding tooling (owner: infra-ops).
- Draft a short candidate-facing FAQ to reduce offer friction.

Appendix: sample mini-postmortem template (one-paragraph format to use during Phase 2):
- What happened?
- Impact (customers, latency, cost).
- Immediate mitigation steps taken.
- Root cause (summary).
- Action items and owners (including rollback thresholds).
- Learnings and monitoring changes.

Notes: This doc intentionally trades speed for safety for hires where mistakes can cascade. It should be adapted for junior roles (shorter phases) and for non-sensitive roles (use standard onboarding).
